title: NetSuite Pricing in 2026: What It Actually Costs
summary: Oracle does not publish NetSuite pricing. The base platform, per-user licenses, add-on modules, implementation, and total cost of ownership, broken down for 2026.
body_markdown:
NetSuite is the most widely used cloud ERP for mid-market companies, and like most enterprise software, Oracle does not publish a price for it. Every deal is a custom quote, and the modular structure, a base platform plus user licenses plus add-on modules plus implementation, means two companies of the same size can pay very different amounts. That makes **NetSuite pricing** hard to plan around. This guide pulls together what third-party trackers and real deals show, so you can size a NetSuite budget before you talk to a rep.


A note on sourcing: Oracle publishes no NetSuite price list, so the figures below come from third-party pricing trackers and partners, and should be treated as directional estimates, not quotes.


## **How much does NetSuite cost?**


> NetSuite pricing is quote-based and modular. Third-party trackers put the base platform around $999 per month at entry, rising to $2,000 to $5,000+ per month for larger editions, plus roughly $99 to $199 per user per month, plus add-on modules and a one-time implementation. All-in, a small deployment often runs about $50,000 to $120,000 in year one, a mid-market one $100,000 to $270,000, and a large multi-entity deployment $350,000 and up.

## **How NetSuite pricing works**


NetSuite is sold as an annual subscription, quoted per deployment, with a roughly 10-user minimum. The number is assembled from:


- **Base platform license.** The core ERP, typically starting near $999 per month and rising by edition.
- **User licenses.** Each full user adds roughly $99 to $199 per month; lighter self-service users cost less.
- **Add-on modules.** Advanced Financials, Revenue Management, Fixed Assets, SuiteBilling, and OneWorld for multi-entity each raise the subscription.
- **Implementation.** A separate, significant one-time cost for configuration, data migration, and integration, done by Oracle or a partner.


Because the price is built layer by layer, the headline base figure understates the real number once you add the users and modules a full finance function needs.


## **NetSuite subscription estimates**


NetSuite does not publish prices, so the clearest picture comes from third-party trackers.[ERP Research](https://www.erpresearch.com/pricing/oracle-netsuite) and[Top10ERP](https://www.top10erp.org/products/netsuite-erp/pricing) report a base platform near $999 per month at entry, full users around $125 per user per month, and implementation starting around $25,000. Trackers note a reported increase in Oracle's user pricing in 2025, pushing per-user figures toward the top of the $99 to $199 range.


Component Estimated cost Source


Base platform (entry) ~$999 / month ERP Research


Base platform (mid to large) ~$2,000 to $5,000+ / month Third-party estimate


Full user license ~$99 to $199 / user / month ERP Research, Top10ERP


Implementation (one-time) ~$25,000 to $500,000+ Third-party estimate


Those are estimates; your quote depends on edition, users, modules, and negotiation. Multi-year commitments are commonly reported to reduce the annual rate.


## **Implementation and total cost of ownership**


Implementation is a separate and significant line. NetSuite deployments involve configuration, data migration, and integration, and are typically run by Oracle or a partner over months. Small projects are often quoted around $25,000 to $50,000, mid-market around $50,000 to $150,000, and large multi-entity OneWorld rollouts $150,000 and well beyond. Add implementation, users, and modules to the base, and realistic all-in first-year totals land near $50,000 to $120,000 for a small deployment, $100,000 to $270,000 for mid-market, and $350,000 or more for large enterprises. For how the ERP fits the wider stack, see[financial systems](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/financial-systems) .


## **What drives NetSuite cost up**


- **Users.** Full user licenses escalate fastest, and Oracle reportedly raised per-user pricing in 2025.
- **Modules.** Each added module, revenue management, OneWorld, warehouse management, or e-commerce, raises the subscription.
- **Multi-entity (OneWorld).** Each additional legal entity or currency adds cost.
- **Customization and implementation scope.** More configuration and integration means a larger one-time bill.
- **Renewals.** Increases of roughly 5% to 15% are commonly reported at renewal unless an uplift cap is negotiated up front.


## **Is NetSuite worth the price?**


For a company that needs a true multi-entity, multi-currency cloud ERP as its system of record, NetSuite often is worth it. It is mature, broad, and scales from mid-market to enterprise, and at that scale a single connected system earns its cost.


The friction is that the modular, per-user model means the bill keeps growing as you add people and capabilities, and much of what finance teams want from the ERP is work, closing the books, reconciling, and reporting, rather than another module to log into.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **Does NetSuite publish its pricing?**


No. Oracle does not publish a NetSuite price list. All pricing is quote-based and modular. The figures here come from third-party trackers such as ERP Research and Top10ERP, not from Oracle.


### **How much does NetSuite cost per year?**


Third-party trackers put a base platform near $999 per month at entry, plus roughly $99 to $199 per user per month and add-on modules, with a one-time implementation. All-in, small deployments often run about $50,000 to $120,000 in year one, mid-market $100,000 to $270,000, and large OneWorld rollouts $350,000 and up.


### **How much does NetSuite implementation cost?**


Implementation is a separate one-time cost, typically around $25,000 to $50,000 for small projects, $50,000 to $150,000 for mid-market, and $150,000 and beyond for large multi-entity deployments, depending on scope, customization, and integrations.


### **Why does NetSuite get expensive?**


Because it is priced by base platform plus users plus modules. Full user licenses escalate fastest, each module adds to the subscription, multi-entity OneWorld adds per-entity cost, and renewals commonly rise 5% to 15% without a negotiated cap.


### **Is NetSuite or Sage Intacct cheaper?**


Both are quote-based, and the answer depends on your size and modules. Sage Intacct often starts lower for a finance-only deployment, with entry core financials near $9,000 to $15,000 a year, while NetSuite is a broader ERP that can cost more as you add users and modules. See our[Sage Intacct pricing](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/sage-intacct-pricing) guide for that breakdown.


## **The bottom line**


NetSuite pricing is modular and quote-only: a base platform near $999 a month at entry, roughly $99 to $199 per user per month, add-on modules, and a significant implementation, with all-in first-year costs from about $50,000 for a small deployment into the hundreds of thousands for large ones. For a company that needs a full cloud ERP, that can be money well spent.
